Source [S2] confirms that Natarajan proposed a disambiguation test for the interior ambiguity and that Marching Cubes 33 was proposed to address topological incoherencies. Both sources support the assertion that standard MC fails to resolve these interior issues and that these specific methods are the proposed solutions.

Using AD alone with the standard 15-case table (or even the 23-case MC23) can still produce non-manifold geometry if interior ambiguities are present [S2][S8].

The claim states that using AD alone with the standard 15-case or 23-case MC tables can produce non-manifold geometry if interior ambiguities are present. Source [S8] explains that AD solves the 'face ambiguity problem' by dictating edge connections on ambiguous faces. However, it also explicitly states that 'the original MC also has an internal ambiguity problem' where linking topologies inside the cube may differ from the trilinear interpolation isosurface. Source [S2] corroborates this by noting that while Nielson and Hamann (AD) resolved face ambiguities, Natarajan observed that 'this ambiguity problem also occurs inside the cube' and that 'even with all the improvements proposed... the meshes generated by the Marching Cubes still had topological incoherencies.' Since AD only addresses face ambiguities (as per S8 and S2) and does not address the interior/topological incoherencies (internal ambiguities) mentioned in both sources, using AD alone with standard tables (which do not account for these interior issues) would indeed leave the geometry with these topological errors (non-manifold geometry). Thus, the evidence supports the claim.
